svg.aria-label: Left: under one joint prompt the cat and dog maps separate because they share a softmax. Right: under two prompts each map has its own softmax and both fill one body. Measured overlap of the top 10 percent is 0.506 to 0.814 for the product and 0.225 to 0.394 for the joint prompt.
svg.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.text: Learn-to-Steer's maps come from one prompt. Ours would come from two.
This is the gap a head trained on joint prompts would have to cross. The heat maps are schematic.
"a cat to the left of a dog"
"a cat" and "a dog", one U-Net pass each
Both words share one softmax at each patch,
so where one wins the other loses.
Each word has a softmax to itself, so nothing
stops both from filling the same body.
Overlap of the top 10% of the cat and dog maps, 1 means the same places (median over 8 seeds, steps 2 to 40):
Measured on SDXL here, with "a cat and a dog" as the joint prompt. Learn-to-Steer never ran on SDXL or on a product of experts.
